articles.title: TikTok announces featured creators for Hispanic Heritage Month
articles.summary: TikTok has launched a series of in-app activations to mark Hispanic Heritage Month, which runs from September 15 to October 15. The centerpiece is a creator showcase featuring figures such as journalist Fernando Hurtado, musician Jasmine Wesley, and comedian Eric Sedeño, chosen to represent storytelling, tradition, and lived experience within Hispanic and Latino communities on the app. TikTok will publish individual interviews with each featured creator through its official TikTok Creators profile, while broader community content will be organized under hashtags including #HispanicTikTok, #LatinTikTok, #HispanicHeritageTikTokContest, and #CasaTikTok. The platform is also running a competition designed to boost user participation and engagement throughout the month-long celebration. TikTok framed the initiative as part of its ongoing effort to highlight historically marginalized groups and demonstrate how the app helps amplify diverse voices and cultural narratives. This year’s push builds on the platform’s broader strategy of using cultural observances to strengthen ties with specific user communities, reinforcing TikTok’s positioning as a space where identity-driven storytelling can reach large, engaged audiences.
articles.li_summary: TikTok kicked off Hispanic Heritage Month (Sept. 15–Oct. 15) by spotlighting creators like journalist Fernando Hurtado, musician Jasmine Wesley and comedian Eric Sedeño, alongside themed hashtags and a new engagement competition.

articles.title: Snapchat report highlights users’ political engagement
articles.summary: Ahead of the November U.S. midterms, Snapchat released a civic engagement report based on an Alter Agents survey of more than 1,000 users aged 18 to 45, aiming to attract political advertisers. The data shows 78% of Snapchat users intend to vote, making them 1.2 times more likely to vote than non-users. Political ads on the platform are influential too: 80% of respondents said promotions introduced them to candidates or causes they didn't previously know, and 74% said ads prompted them to research candidates further. Peer influence remains strong, with 66% discovering political information through close social circles and 64% trusting peer perspectives over traditional news outlets. Snapchat users are also 1.4 times more likely than non-users to engage with cause- or candidate-related ads, at 83%. This builds on Snapchat's history of voter mobilization efforts, having driven 450,000 voter registrations in 2018 and 1.2 million in 2020 through in-app prompts, reinforcing its case as a valuable channel for political outreach.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat published a new report from Alter Agents, surveying over 1,000 users aged 18-45, showing 78% plan to vote in the midterms and 83% actively engage with political ads, as it pitches itself for election ad spend.

articles.title: Meta adds more creator partnership tools
articles.summary: On Tuesday, Meta officially launched its Creator Marketing hub, first previewed in June, merging brand-creator discovery and outreach into a single platform. New features include discovery filters with predicted affiliate content search, objective-based content recommendations, one-click ad creation from creator listings, content-level permissions with expiration dates, and ad editing tools letting brands remove copyrighted music or stickers from creator content. Partnership messaging is now built directly into the hub, so brands can move from discov
articles.li_summary: Meta launched its Creator Marketing hub on Tuesday, consolidating discovery, outreach, and ad-creation tools into one interface, while also expanding creator APIs and rolling out Instagram live video ads on September 29.

articles.title: Meta announces Edits Plus paid subscription tier
articles.summary: Meta is building a paid subscription tier called Edits Plus for its Edits video editing app, which competes with ByteDance's CapCut. The tier was revealed in a slide from a broader announcement about Meta's new Meta One Business subscription packages, and will be offered either bundled within those business packages or as its own standalone subscription. Edits Plus will give users more storage for video projects and expanded access to Meta's AI-powered editing features, addressing capacity limits that currently restrict heavy users. Meta has long signaled it would eventually monetize AI add-ons within Edits, and Instagram chief Adam Mosseri explained in a July Stories Q&A that the AI models powering these tools are costly to run, so free access is currently capped by daily usage limits, with a subscription option in development to unlock higher usage caps. Meta has not disclosed pricing details or specified what the new usage thresholds will be once Edits Plus launches, leaving exact costs and limits still unknown.
articles.li_summary: Meta is developing "Edits Plus," a paid subscription tier for its Edits video editing app that offers expanded storage and greater access to AI-powered editing tools, available standalone or via Meta One Business packages.

articles.title: Meta launches Meta One for Business add-on packages
articles.summary: Meta introduced Meta One for Business, a new subscription lineup for brands, priced across tiers from $14.99 to $499 per month, bundling AI-powered tools, analytics and content features across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Higher tiers unlock competitive insights comparing up to 10 rival brands on Instagram, extended audience history data beyond the current 90-day limit, and custom audience insights showing non-followers who engage with content on Facebook. Content scheduling gets upgraded with posting-time recommendations and bulk Instagram uploads. A long-requested feature, links within Instagram posts and Reels, arrives in limited form: Advanced subscribers ($49.99/month) get 4 links each for posts and Reels monthly, Expert subscribers ($149) get 8, and Max subscribers ($499) get 12. Other perks include a bold Facebook Follow button for visibility, Verified Channels on WhatsApp, and a new AI chatbot called Meta business agent that answers customer messages on WhatsApp Business around the clock and offers engagement and lead-generation guidance. This expands Meta's subscription business, which already reportedly includes around 35 million Meta Verified users generating roughly $2 billion annually.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Meta One for Business, a tiered subscription line from $14.99 to $499 monthly offering AI tools, competitor insights on up to 10 brands, and limited Instagram post links.

articles.title: How Carter’s is refreshing its brand to reach Gen Z, millennial parents
articles.summary: Carter's is rolling out its first logo update since 2000 alongside a new brand campaign, "Watch Them Glow," debuting September 15 with a 60-second spot airing on Nexxen, Roku, Disney+, Hulu, and the brand's own digital and social channels. The redesign replaces the apostrophe in "Carter's" with a shooting star symbolizing individuality, paired with a script inspired by the company's earlier logos. The campaign, built around the tagline "let every child's light shine," is meant to resonate with Gen Z and young millennial parents who prioritize brand values and self-expression, according to CMO Sarah Crockett, citing Pew Research data showing nearly half of U.S. parents are raising kids differently than they were raised. Supporting the refresh is a new creator initiative called Light Makers, plus a Glow Grants program that will award up to 15 grants in its first year across the U.S. and Canada. Additional packaging, retail, and product updates are planned for 2027. The push follows Carter's Inc.'s decision to increase marketing spend this year, which executives credit for a 5% net sales increase in Q2 2026.
articles.li_summary: Carter's is launching a brand refresh and "Watch Them Glow" campaign on Sept. 15, featuring a new logo with a shooting-star apostrophe, a 60-second CTV spot, and a creator program called Light Makers to attract Gen Z and millennial parents.

articles.title: Reddit shares holiday shopping insights
articles.summary: Reddit has published fresh insights into how its users approach holiday shopping and celebration planning, highlighting the platform's growing role as a research tool for gift-buying decisions. The data comes as Reddit becomes an increasingly important consideration for marketers, driven by both its expanding user base and its frequent citation as a source in AI chatbot responses like ChatGPT's. This positions Reddit as a potential touchpoint for reaching consumers during their research process. However, the platform recently experienced a notable decline in referral traffic from ChatGPT last month, as tracked by Promptwatch, raising questions about how AI tools are directing users to the site. Despite this dip, Reddit's reputation for authentic, user-generated product discussions continues to make it a trusted destination for shoppers navigating an AI-influenced search landscape, with more people turning to the platform directly for real-world purchasing advice rather than relying solely on AI-generated summaries during the holiday shopping season.
articles.li_summary: Reddit released new holiday shopping data showing how users research gifts and plan celebrations on the platform, even as ChatGPT referral traffic to Reddit dropped sharply last month according to Promptwatch.

articles.title: X continues to host CSAM content
articles.summary: New research from the Canadian Center for Child Protection, reported by the New York Times, reveals that X continues to struggle with child sexual abuse material three years after Elon Musk vowed to make eradicating CSAM his top priority following the 2022 Twitter acquisition. The investigation found X's Grok chatbot has been used to generate CSAM, while separate Times testing showed users still sharing CSAM on the platform, including content previously flagged by authorities. This follows an earlier controversy this year when users exploited Grok to create nudified deepfake images, with reports indicating some depicted minors; X says it has since restricted this Grok functionality, though testing suggests workarounds remain possible. X currently faces a lawsuit from sexual abuse survivors alleging Grok was trained on known CSAM, enabling further exploitation. Separately, X has opposed proposed legislation banning nudification technology, arguing it violates constitutional free speech protections. The pattern suggests X's commitment to free expression continues to complicate its stated efforts to remove harmful content, leaving CSAM issues largely unresolved despite years of public pledges.
articles.li_summary: A Canadian Center for Child Protection investigation and New York Times testing found X still hosts CSAM material, with Grok chatbot enabling generation of such content despite Musk's 2022 pledge to make eliminating CSAM "Priority #1."

articles.title: LinkedIn shares tips on Thought Leader ads
articles.summary: LinkedIn has released tips for marketers on maximizing its Thought Leader Ads format, which lets brands amplify authentic, positive posts and comments from users to strengthen brand messaging and improve campaign responses. The feature originally applied only to employee content but was expanded in March 2025 to include posts from any user, and LinkedIn added a version for event promotion in August 2025. The platform is pushing this guidance because of strong performance data: LinkedIn has reported that 71% of decision-makers consider thought leadership content more persuasive than standard advertising formats, and B2B marketers using Thought Leader Ads have seen engagement rates 1.6 times higher than those achieved with single-image ad promotions. By leaning on individual endorsements rather than polished corporate messaging, brands can tap into perceived authenticity to influence potential customers earlier in the buying process. The new tips are aimed at helping marketers structure these campaigns more effectively, offering practical direction for teams looking to capitalize on user-generated content as part of their broader LinkedIn advertising and B2B marketing strategies.
articles.li_summary: LinkedIn published new guidance on optimizing Thought Leader Ads, its format that boosts user-generated posts, citing 71% of decision-makers rating thought leadership more persuasive than traditional advertising.

articles.title: Pinterest announces new deal with Nvidia
articles.summary: Pinterest has deepened its existing partnership with Nvidia to upgrade the AI infrastructure behind its visual search and discovery features. The new setup runs on Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs and Dynamo platform, combined with Pinterest's own visual embeddings, giving internal teams a shared infrastructure for launching multimodal AI products instead of building custom systems for each one. Pinterest says the upgrade lets it convert over 80 billion monthly searches into stronger signals for AI-powered discovery and shopping, and allows its Pinterest Assistant tool to process 25 times more visual context per request. Benchmark testing showed using precomputed visual representations, rather than repeatedly analyzing raw images, cut response startup time by roughly 85x and improved overall latency by about 7.3x. The updated system is also meant to strengthen content understanding and safety systems as visual search expands. This builds on Pinterest's broader long-term agreement with Nvidia aimed at advancing conversational and visual AI experiences, positioning the platform for more personalized, data-driven search and shopping performance going forward.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest expanded its Nvidia partnership, using Blackwell GPUs and Dynamo to power AI-driven visual search, cutting response startup time by 85x and overall latency by 7.3x in benchmark tests.

articles.title: Old Navy’s MrBeast deal boosts engagement amid bigger bet on creators
articles.summary: Old Navy launched its first back-to-school campaign anchored by a single creator, partnering with MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson) as part of a new multiyear deal, and the results are an early bright spot amid a sales slump—comparable sales fell 4% in Q2. The campaign, mixing comedic content, sweepstakes, and student-focused giveaways like a year of free lunches for a Kansas middle school, generated over 100 million global YouTube views and 1.4 billion impressions while lifting traffic to Old Navy's kids' assortment page by more than 22% right after launch, according to data shared with Marketing Dive. Gap Inc. SVP Damon Berger said the approach favors authentic storytelling over the brand's traditionally polished ad style. Gap Inc. CEO Richard Dickson also cited a Cardi B denim campaign as evidence of improved marketing execution, though sales impact won't be confirmed until next earnings. The push aligns with broader industry moves toward creator-led marketing targeting Gen Z and Gen Alpha, with 91% of parents in a HarrisX/Allison Worldwide survey saying teens influence household brand choices. Old Navy plans to expand creator content through the holiday season, following CEO transition from Haio Barbeito to Michael Francis.
articles.li_summary: Old Navy's back-to-school campaign with MrBeast drove a 22% jump in kids' assortment web traffic and generated over 100 million YouTube views and 1.4 billion impressions.

articles.title: Meta highlights creation tools for AI glasses
articles.summary: Meta has publicized new creation features exclusive to its AI-enabled glasses, first previewed back in June, in an apparent effort to spotlight the device's value amid mounting criticism. Spin view lets viewers experience more of a captured video by physically turning their own device, mimicking the original recording motion. Multi-cam syncs footage from a user's phone and their Meta glasses simultaneously, letting audiences see both angles in one clip. Instagram also gained new glasses-specific editing tools, giving users more options to revise footage after capture. The push comes as Meta faces growing backlash over privacy misuse, with reports showing some wearers disabling the glasses' recording indicator light to secretly film people, later posting that footage online without consent. This has triggered regulatory investigations in multiple regions and inspired activist pushback, including anti-AI-glasses posters created by the group Radical Graffiti and displayed throughout London's Underground stations. Despite the controversy, Meta says it hasn't seen any measurable drop in glasses sales and continues promoting the hardware's creative capabilities to users.
articles.li_summary: Meta rolled out new AI-glasses creation tools—spin view, multi-cam syncing with phones, and Instagram editing features—first previewed in June, even as backlash grows over wearers disabling recording lights to film people without consent.

articles.title: New images show Meta’s next-gen virtual reality device
articles.summary: A newly surfaced firmware clip has given the first look at Meta's upcoming Phoenix mixed reality headset, spotted by VR researcher @Lunayian within the HorizonOS Prescription Lens package and reported by Road to VR. Phoenix appears to be positioned as the successor to Meta's Quest VR line, suggesting the company hasn't fully stepped away from VR despite its pivot toward AI-powered wearables. Phoenix is one of several hardware projects reportedly in Meta's pipeline, alongside Hypernova, an upgraded version of its current AI smart glasses, and Aria, a bulkier AR device designed to house more advanced components. Meta appears to be integrating AI more deeply into its VR roadmap as the technology matures. However, the company's broader glasses strategy faces headwinds: its recording-enabled AI glasses have drawn backlash over privacy misuse, prompting bans in some venues and regulatory scrutiny in multiple regions, which could force design changes and affect sales. Despite these challenges, Meta continues developing lighter, more capable AR, VR, and AI devices, with more details expected at its Meta Connect event later this month.
articles.li_summary: VR researcher @Lunayian leaked footage from Meta's HorizonOS Prescription Lens firmware revealing "Phoenix," a next-generation mixed reality headset that appears to succeed the current Quest VR lineup, alongside other in-development devices like Hypernova AI glasses.

articles.title: Threads might be bigger than X, says Zuckerberg
articles.summary: In a recent interview with Sources, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg claimed Threads has caught up to or surpassed X in size, despite launching years after Elon Musk's platform. Threads hit 500 million monthly active users in June 2025, while X's own SpaceX investment prospectus put its figure at 550 million MAU in May, up from 520 million the prior December—numbers that conflict with Musk's May 2024 claim of 600 million users, suggesting either a steep decline or earlier exaggeration. X has also reported shrinking usage across the EU recently. Zuckerberg noted he still personally posts identical content on both platforms since each hosts distinct communities, specifically citing AI industry figures who remain active on X. The comparison highlights how Meta has again used a rival's format, echoing its earlier replication of Snapchat's Stories feature, to build a competing product that now rivals X's scale, making Threads a legitimate consideration in advertisers' social media strategies alongside X.
articles.li_summary: Mark Zuckerberg told the Sources podcast that Threads is now bigger than X or about to be, citing Threads' 500 million monthly active users in June versus X's reported 550 million.

articles.title: YouTube report examines mainstream culture
articles.summary: YouTube released a Trends and Culture report exploring how mainstream culture is evolving alongside expanded internet access and niche online communities. Based on an NRG survey of 939 people aged 14 to 44, the report found that 63% of respondents said they're more likely now than five years ago to watch content or follow creators that their peers also follow, showing that shared cultural experiences still matter despite fragmentation. Notably, 77% of respondents viewed YouTube creators and 78% viewed memes as widely recognized, nearly matching the 79% who said the same about Hollywood celebrities and 83% for the Super Bowl. YouTube identified three signals now defining mainstream status: visibility, participation, and sustained conversation, noting that ideas typically need all three to break through. The report also found that 82% of 14- to 24-year-olds use YouTube to engage with fandoms or topics they follow, with 95% of that group returning weekly. Examples cited include "Backrooms" and "Five Nights at Freddy's," both of which grew from YouTube content into major films, and creator MrBeast, illustrating YouTube's expanding role as a cultural gatekeeper.
articles.li_summary: YouTube's new Trends and Culture report, based on an NRG survey of 939 people aged 14-44, finds 63% now follow creators or content their peers also follow, with YouTube creators and memes rated as culturally recognizable as Hollywood celebrities and the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Sociable: YouTube expands Watch With to more creators
articles.summary: YouTube is expanding testing of Watch With, a feature first introduced in 2024 alongside its NFL livestream coverage, to a broader group of creators. Eligible users in the experiment group now see a "React live" button in the Share panel when viewing qualifying livestreams on mobile, allowing them to record and broadcast their own reactions in real time alongside the original broadcast. The reacting creator's phone camera automatically locks into horizontal orientation and cannot be switched off during the session. Viewers, regardless of device, see a combined vertical stream showing both the original content and the reactor's camera feed. Creators can monetize these reaction streams normally and gain access to shared viewing metrics with the original broadcaster. This rollout fits into YouTube's broader push to boost live engagement, alongside other tests like gamified livestream leaderboards and 24/7 "livestream stations." YouTube noted that as of September 2025, over 30% of daily logged-in users were watching live content, underscoring the platform's growing focus on interactive, real-time viewing experiences.
articles.li_summary: YouTube is widening access to its Watch With feature, letting more eligible creators broadcast live reaction videos alongside original livestreams via a "React live" button, with revenue sharing and combined viewer metrics.

articles.title: Snapchat promises advertisers faster conversions for the holidays
articles.summary: Snapchat has introduced the Commerce Power Pack, a bundle of performance-marketing tools aimed at boosting holiday-season advertiser results, built around claims that the platform converts purchases half a day faster than other major social networks, per TransUnion data. The suite expands Dynamic Product Ads into Sponsored Snaps, letting brands place AI-recommended catalog products directly inside Chat, Snapchat's most-used feature, and is available globally now. Also included: Value Optimization (in beta), which targets return on ad spend; Third-Party Web Optimization (open beta), which blends first- and third-party data and showed 23% lower third-party cost-per-purchase and 37% higher ROAS in Google Analytics testing; and Omnichannel Optimization (alpha), which optimizes purchases across app and web within one campaign. Snap will market these tools via a "Spend Smarter" campaign launching in the US and UK this month. The announcement follows the departure of Chief Business Officer Ajit Mohan, replaced by new Chief Commercial Officer Ronan Harris, formerly EMEA business lead. Snap's Q2 revenue rose 19% year-over-year to $1.6 billion, with ad revenue up 9%.
articles.li_summary: Snapchat unveiled the Commerce Power Pack, a holiday advertising suite adding Dynamic Product Ads in Chat, Value Optimization, Third-Party Web Optimization, and Omnichannel Optimization, citing TransUnion data showing conversions half a day faster than rival platforms.

articles.title: Why Bonobos’ fall campaign centers on episodic content with Jack Quaid
articles.summary: Bonobos debuted its fall marketing campaign on Thursday, anchored by "The Weekday Warrior Show," a scripted episodic series starring actor Jack Quaid, known for "The Boys" and "Companion." In the first episode, Quaid plays a self-declared "weekday warrior consultant" who breaks the fourth wall to joke about office life while promoting the brand's best-selling Weekday Warrior Pant, described by CMO Joe Berean as combining dress-pant polish with chino comfort. The series uses a laugh track and office setting to mimic classic sitcoms, while incorporating real Bonobos employees for authenticity. Designed as a digital- and social-first format, the campaign will roll out further episodes highlighting other fall items, including the Weekday Warrior Dress Shirt, Jetsetter Dress Shirt, Everyday Oxford Shirt, Unconstructed Blazer and Knit Blazer, with supplemental video content on the brand's website. The collection is sold online and across Bonobos' 48 U.S. guideshops, and the brand plans to relaunch on Shopify soon. Bonobos, founded in 2007 and now owned by Phoenix Retail after a 2024 bankruptcy sale, has also worked this year with celebrities like Nicholas Braun and Carl Radke as part of a broader "wry smile" brand positioning.
articles.li_summary: Bonobos launched a fall campaign built around "The Weekday Warrior Show," an episodic sitcom-style content series starring Jack Quaid that promotes the brand's Weekday Warrior Pant across digital and social channels throughout the season.

articles.title: Instagram Chief warns against eliminating algorithms
articles.summary: Instagram Chief Adam Mosseri briefed Australian journalists this week, arguing that removing content-ranking algorithms would make the platform less engaging and harm creators who depend on algorithmic reach to find audiences. His comments follow an Australian government plan, currently in consultation, to restrict engagement-driven algorithms in social apps, potentially forcing platforms toward chronological feeds to combat harmful content and addictive usage. Mosseri claimed that without ranking, feeds would fill with content from the most frequent posters—brands, businesses, and news publishers—crowding out friends and creators, ultimately shrinking overall engagement and available reach for everyone. He made similar points in a recent Instagram post, and separately used the briefing to launch "Algo Confessions," a new Australian content series featuring celebrities discussing how algorithms shape their app experience. Mosseri also dismissed support for chronological feeds as coming from only a "vocal minority," predicting users would regret such a shift. However, the reduced engagement and usage he warns against may actually align with regulators' stated goals of curbing addictive social media behavior and limiting exposure to harmful content among Australian users.
articles.li_summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri warned that Australia's proposed laws restricting engagement-driven algorithms would shrink reach for creators and push feeds toward chronological, business-and-publisher-heavy content, calling it a net negative for users.

articles.title: X rolls out number code access for DMs
articles.summary: X has begun rolling out a new number code system within its updated X Chat messaging feature, allowing users to generate a unique 10-digit "X number" that can be shared to grant DM access to people who aren't mutual followers. Anyone visiting a profile who wants to message that user but doesn't already follow them will need to enter this code to unlock the conversation, which also enables audio and video calling once access is granted. Users can refresh or change their code at any time, giving them ongoing control over exactly who can reach them and allowing access to be revoked simply by generating a new number. This sits alongside X Chat's existing settings, where users can already choose to receive DMs from followers only or open messages to everyone. The code system adds a middle-ground option, useful for scenarios like temporarily inviting event attendees to message after a gathering, or letting public figures grant selected fans time-limited DM access before deactivating the code. The rollout is ongoing and not yet available to all users.
articles.li_summary: X is rolling out a feature letting X Chat users generate a unique 10-digit "X number" code that non-followers can enter to unlock DM, audio, and video call access without sharing phone numbers.

articles.title: Meta expands Community Notes to Latin America
articles.summary: Meta has quietly updated its Community Notes explainer page to confirm it is testing the crowdsourced fact-checking program in 16 Latin American countries: Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, and Venezuela. Users there can now sign up as contributors, though notes won't be published publicly until Meta deems the system reliable, at which point it plans to phase out third-party fact-checking in those markets, mirroring its January 2025 U.S. shift. Meta has cited a reported 50% drop in enforcement mistakes since launching Community Notes domestically as evidence of success, though critics note this could simply reflect reduced moderation overall, since notes only display when contributors across opposing political viewpoints agree, meaning most notes never get shown even when flagging real misinformation. Meta's own Oversight Board flagged concerns on Thursday, warning that countries with disinformation networks, political violence, or high-risk elections could see real harm from the model, and it had asked Meta to share country-specific risk assessments before expanding, something Meta appears not to have done.
articles.li_summary: Meta is expanding its crowdsourced Community Notes fact-checking test to 16 Latin American countries, including Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, and Venezuela, ahead of a possible full rollout replacing third-party fact-checkers there.

articles.title: Caesars gives NFL legend a ‘looksmaxxing’ makeover in sportsbook ads
articles.summary: Caesars Sportsbook debuted "We've Had Some Work Done," a national campaign launched Wednesday to coincide with the NFL season opener and Clay Matthews' Sept. 10 debut as a Netflix sportscaster. The 15- and 30-second spots feature Matthews sporting an exaggerated "looksmaxxing" transformation, complete with an oversized jawline and inflated calf muscles, achieved through practical prosthetics and makeup from Legacy Effects rather than AI or digital filters. The makeover serves as a metaphor for the sportsbook's own overhaul since its 2021 launch, highlighting a redesigned app, new rewards system and features like Flex Parlays. Created with minority-owned agency Fellow Kids and produced by Hungry Man under director Dave Laden, the campaign was teased by TMZ beforehand to generate viral buzz, echoing tactics used in CeraVe's Michael Cera push. Caesars SVP Samira Zebian said the goal was making the app's evolution "impossible to miss" as the brand competes against DraftKings and FanDuel in the crowded sports betting market. The campaign will run across TV, digital and social channels throughout the football season.
articles.li_summary: Caesars Sportsbook launched "We've Had Some Work Done," a new ad campaign featuring ex-NFL star Clay Matthews with an exaggerated "looksmaxxing" makeover, promoting app redesigns and features like Flex Parlays ahead of the NFL season.

articles.title: X adds new anti-lawsuit provision to terms of service
articles.summary: X revised its Terms of Service on Wednesday, requiring all users to accept the new terms to keep using the platform. Legal disputes will now be handled specifically in Texas courts under Texas law, reflecting X's ties to SpaceX, which is headquartered there. The update also sharpens user-responsibility language, stating users are accountable for actions taken through features that act autonomously on their behalf, echoing Elon Musk's past comments about personal liability for illegal content generated via xAI tools. Most notably, X added explicit language stating users waive their right to a jury trial and to join or bring class, collective, or representative actions, extending this to corporate affiliates where legally allowed. This comes as X faces a class action from sexual abuse survivors alleging xAI's Grok chatbot generated and distributed child sexual abuse material, with one plaintiff claiming Grok was trained using existing CSAM tied to them. Similar waivers already exist at Twitter, Meta, and TikTok, and haven't historically stopped class actions, so enforceability of X's updated clause remains uncertain.
articles.li_summary: X updated its Terms of Service on Wednesday, adding explicit jury-trial and class-action waivers for all users, requiring Texas courts under Texas law, amid an active lawsuit alleging Grok generated CSAM.

articles.title: Meta keeps trying to make digital assistants happen
articles.summary: Meta released Muse, a new AI-powered chatbot app that lets users name their assistant, converse with it, and assign tasks it can complete autonomously in the background, positioning it as Mark Zuckerberg's latest step toward "personal superintelligence for everyone." This mirrors Meta's 2015 "M" assistant, which former Messenger chief David Marcus said could book restaurants, arrange travel, and purchase gifts, but which was discontinued in January 2018 after failing to attract sustained user interest. Meta also previously tried celebrity-themed chatbots and Messenger bots in 2016, none of which gained traction despite heavy promotion. Zuckerberg described his own use of Muse as wanting help to "be a better father and a better husband" and show up more for friends, revealing an optimization-driven mindset toward maximizing efficiency in daily life. Critics argue this reflects a mismatch with most users, who value human interaction and everyday tasks like shopping or research as meaningful experiences rather than inefficiencies to eliminate, suggesting Muse may repeat the same underwhelming reception as Meta's earlier assistant products.
articles.li_summary: Meta launched its Muse AI assistant app this week, letting users name and delegate background tasks to a chatbot, echoing its failed 2015 "M" personal assistant that was shelved in January 2018 due to low adoption.

articles.title: Pinterest shares insights into men’s trends
articles.summary: Pinterest released a trend breakdown covering men's search behavior heading into 2026, aimed at helping marketers refine targeting as men now represent roughly a third of the platform's 640 million monthly active users. The report groups rising interests into themes: wellness and travel resets like "wellness retreats" (+83%) and "road trip ideas" (+126%); active social outings such as "Hyrox" (+193%) and "padel event" (+47%); hands-on hobbies including "easy woodworking projects" (+316%) and "junk journaling ideas" (+214%); home entertaining touches like "charcuterie board design" (+390%) and "record player setup" (+223%); grooming and beauty shifts such as "Italian beard fade" (+725%) and "modern wolf cut men" (+553%); nail color trends including "silver nails men" (+87%); skincare growth with overall men's product searches up 280% and "red light mask" (+156%); fragrance interest via "perfume discovery set" (+167%); and fashion movements spanning workwear-inspired looks, leather goods like "handmade leather wallet" (+290%), and pink clothing items such as "dusty pink shirt outfit men" (+283%). Pinterest frames these shifts as a roadmap for brands building Pin ad campaigns targeting male users.
articles.li_summary: Pinterest published its 2026 men's trend report, highlighting search spikes like "Italian beard fade" (+725%), "modern wolf cut men" (+553%) and "charcuterie board design" (+390%), as men now make up a third of its 640 million monthly users.

articles.title: Snap CEO discusses ad development and AI
articles.summary: In a letter marking Snap's 15th anniversary, CEO Evan Spiegel laid out the company's advertising roadmap, centered on what he calls "generative advertising." Rather than relying on explicit intent signals like search queries or cart additions, Spiegel wants AI-driven multimodal models to analyze user behavior and friend connections to predict what people might want next, then match them with relevant businesses, potentially generating new demand instead of just capturing existing intent. He also highlighted creator partnerships as a growing ad opportunity, noting creator-made ads are watched 25% longer and generate 16% more active attention than standard branding ads, with over 300,000 creators now eligible for brand collaborations. Spiegel additionally plans to make product discovery and sharing easier within the app, organically surfacing shopping-related content to drive purchases. Beyond advertising, Spiegel criticized unnamed "ruthless competitors" for copying Snapchat's features and pushed back against grouping Snapchat with broader "social media," citing studies linking Snapchat use to improved friendship closeness, peer support, and overall wellbeing, though he acknowledged these findings show correlation rather than proven causation.
articles.li_summary: Snap CEO Evan Spiegel used a 15th-anniversary staff letter to unveil plans for "generative advertising," using AI to predict user desires and recommend products before they search, while touting creator ads' 25% longer play time and 16% higher attention versus standard brand ads.

articles.title: Meta launches Muse personal AI
articles.summary: Meta has released Muse, a new AI agent app and in-stream chatbot integrated with users' Facebook and Instagram profiles, letting people name their own assistant and delegate tasks such as trip planning, ticket booking, email sending, and form completion. Muse can also complete purchases directly within conversations, raising data-privacy concerns
articles.li_summary: Meta launched Muse, a personal AI agent app that plans tasks, books travel, fills out forms, and completes in-stream purchases, running on a dedicated "Muse Secure VM" co-designed with Signal's Moxie Marlinspike, with 100 million free weekly tokens per user.
